newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates steady in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates steady in liquid market.

text.p: ------------------------Nov 28------------------------------ * Market seen liquid despite Central Bank's dollar sales

Philippine interbank call loan rates were steady on Thursday at an average of 10.8125 percent, a mere 1/16 percent higher than the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate of 10.75 percent, traders said.
"The market is so liquid," a trader from a big bank said, since banks were injected with 5.1 billion pesos from matured Treasury bills last Wednesday and 4.9 billion in T-notes early in the week.
Dut to the lack of borrowers among banks, volume thinned to 5.094 billion from 11.281 billion pesos.
"Banks would rather lend to the Central Bank. It's less paperwork," said the same dealer.
Done rates ranged from 10.875 to 10.78125 percent, with 18 lenders and 15 borrowers.
Dealers believe the market would remain liquid on Friday even if banks would be drained of some 1.8 billion pesos after buying dollars from Central Bank early in the day.
"The liquidity is still sufficient," one trader said.
In the secondary market trading of T-bills, dealers said buying focus was on the two-year Treasury notes where rates hardly changed.
"The effective yield could be lower," if banks focused on the short-term bills where interest rates had started to slide, a trader said.
The three-month bills had a bid rate of 11.55 to 11.75 percent; the six months, 12.15 to 12.375 percent; the one year, 12.60 to 12.75 percent, dealers said.
